newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Gold Peak's Clipsal stake drops.
newsitem.headline: Gold Peak's Clipsal stake drops.

text.p: Electrical fittings firm Clipsal Industries Holdings Ltd said on Monday it has placed nine million new shares or 9.2 percent of its issued share capital at US$3.79 each today.
The price represented a 2.8-percent discount to the closing price of US$3.90 on May 30, 1997, a company statement said.
It said the net proceeds of US$33.5 million would be used to expand its business and to provide additional working capital.
Clipsal's parent company, Gold Peak Industries Holdings Ltd, also announced in the statement it had exercised six million Clipsal warrants for new shares at a subscription price of US$2.03 each.
It also sold three million existing Clipsal shares to Peregrine Brokerage Ltd at US$3.79 each. Both transactions took place on May 30, 1997.
After the issue of the new Clipsal shares, Gold Peak's shareholding in Clipsal will change to 46 percent from 50.1 percent, making Clipsal an associated company instead of a major subsidiary.
Trading in shares of the battery and electronic component maker Gold Peak was suspended in Hong Kong earlier today.
Gold Peak intends to use its US$11.4 million proceeds as additional working capital.
Peregrine Securities Singapore Pte Ltd and Pergrine Capital Ltd are the placement agents.
